Third-party code served to the plugin sandbox (unmodified; byte-identical to the Android assets in
app/src/main/resources/liuying-plugin-modules/, which a unit test checks):

  cheerio.js    cheerio-without-node-native 0.20.2, MIT license
                bundled with its dependencies htmlparser2, css-select, domutils, entities and lodash (all MIT)
                https://github.com/oyyd/cheerio-without-node-native
  crypto-js.js  crypto-js 4.2.0, MIT license, Evan Vosberg
                https://github.com/brix/crypto-js

Both are esbuild bundles. The license and attribution comments of the original packages are kept inside the files.
These modules are only ever loaded when a plugin calls require() on the exact package name; they run inside the sandbox
worker, never in the Liuying page.
